abstract_nepberta: NepBERTa also outperforms the character model at every size, but it is less sample-efficient than XLM-R between 100 and 2,500 examples, and the two are indistinguishable from 5,000 examples upward. Nepali-specific pretraining therefore does not improve data efficiency on this task.
full_nepberta_paragraph: NepBERTa reaches {full_nepberta} ({full_nepberta_ci}) at full size. Its paired difference from XLM-R, XLM-R minus NepBERTa, is {test_xlmr_vs_nepberta_diff} ({test_xlmr_vs_nepberta_ci}; Holm-adjusted p = {test_xlmr_vs_nepberta_p}), so the two transformers cannot be distinguished on macro F1. The McNemar counts ({test_xlmr_vs_nepberta_mc}) show that XLM-R is correct more often. This is consistent with its higher accuracy ({full_xlmr_acc} versus {full_nepberta_acc}) and NepBERTa's better neutral-class F1 ({full_nepberta_neutral} versus {full_xlmr_neutral}). Accuracy and macro F1 weight these trade-offs differently.
conclusion_nepberta: A Nepali monolingual encoder, NepBERTa, is no more sample-efficient than XLM-R. It trails XLM-R between 100 and 2,500 examples and matches it from 5,000 upward.
